t: Saladin rose in the service of the Zengid ruler Nur al-Din, became vizier of Fatimid Egypt in 1169 and two years later ended the Fatimid Caliphate.
After Nur al-Din's death in 1174 he took Damascus and then most of Muslim Syria and Upper Mesopotamia, largely at the expense of his former master's family.
His victory at Hattin and capture of Jerusalem in 1187 provoked the Third Crusade, which ended in 1192 with Jerusalem still in his hands.
dyk: At his death Saladin had in his possession one piece of gold and forty pieces of silver; he had given away his wealth to his poor subjects and left nothing to pay for his funeral.
ev: Saladin is born in Tikrit, by his biographer's account on the night his family left the town
The Fatimid caliph al-Adid appoints him vizier of Egypt after the death of his uncle Shirkuh
Al-Adid dies and the Abbasid caliph is proclaimed in Cairo, ending the Fatimid Caliphate
After Nur al-Din's death he rides to Damascus with 700 horsemen and enters it amid general acclamation
He defeats the Zengids at the Horns of Hama and is declared Sultan of Egypt and Syria
He largely annihilates the Crusader army at Hattin and Jerusalem capitulates to him
The Treaty of Jaffa with Richard I ends the Third Crusade
He dies of a fever at Damascus

f.born: c. 1137 in Tikrit, in present-day Iraq, to a family of Kurdish Rawadiya ancestry; son of Najm al-Din Ayyub, warden of the fortress of Tikrit
f.died: 4 March 1193 (27 Safar 589 AH) at Damascus, of a fever; buried in a mausoleum in the garden outside the Umayyad Mosque
f.role: Vizier of Fatimid Egypt from 26 March 1169; ruler of Egypt after the end of the Fatimid Caliphate in 1171; declared Sultan of Egypt and Syria by the Abbasid caliph in 1175; founder of the Ayyubid dynasty
f.known: Founding the Ayyubid dynasty; abolishing the Fatimid Caliphate; uniting Egypt and Syria under one ruler; the victory at Hattin in 1187; the capture of Jerusalem; the war against Richard I in the Third Crusade; a reputation for generosity in Muslim and Christian sources
